title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed into a known high-traffic scenario—a major public celebration near the Golden Gate Bridge—without sufficient battery reserves to handle the actual congestion that occurred. The system was built and tested under normal traffic conditions, not during the extreme, multi-hour gridlock that followed Fourth of July fireworks. At least a dozen vehicles ran out of power and required towing, leaving them immobile on streets while human drivers were stuck around them.

The deployment failure was in operational planning rather than the autonomous driving system itself. Waymo attributed the problem to unplanned road closures and unexpected congestion, which suggests the company did not model or stress-test for the realistic traffic patterns of a major event in that location. One vehicle also caught fire after driving over fireworks on the road, showing the system did not avoid or stop for hazards posed by celebratory activity.

It is not established whether Waymo had advance warning of the event's scale, whether the vehicles were pre-positioned with full charge, or what specific improvements the company will implement for future major events.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles ran out of battery power and required towing during heavy traffic congestion in San Francisco on Saturday following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations near the Golden Gate Bridge. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets. The company attributed the issue to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries were reported. Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the stranded vehicles, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to improve its resilience during major traffic disruptions.

Frustrated residents reported being stuck in standstill traffic for nearly two hours while frustrated motorists yelled at the driverless cars with no operators present. One passenger described a Waymo continuing to drive while someone set off fireworks in the road. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie warned residents about post-fireworks traffic and asked for patience while streets cleared. His office indicated it will hold conversations with public and private partners to improve traffic management for future large events after more than 100,000 people experienced delays leaving the area.
